points.text: The Selic was cut to 13.75% on 16 September, the fifth straight quarter-point cut from 15%.
September's IPCA-15 surprised higher at 0.70%, and 12-month inflation is 4.47%, just under the 4.5% ceiling.
The external position is strong. Reserves were $368.9bn in July.
The 12-month current account deficit was 2.71% of GDP through March.
This is the core issue for Brazil. Gross debt reached 82.5% of GDP in July, the highest since April 2021.
Twelve-month interest costs total 8.67% of GDP. The 12-month nominal deficit reached 9.99% of GDP in June.
No IMF programme. Domestic funding runs through NTN-Fs (fixed-rate), NTN-Bs (IPCA-linked) and LFTs (Selic-linked). The curve section in Valuation below comes straight from Tesouro Direto every day.
One EM strategist moved Brazil USD sovereigns to Underweight as a valuation call, arguing spreads have richened to near one-year tights while fiscal evidence has not improved.
DI futures (B3) have no free API. Add DI levels to the bonds list by hand, and use the Tesouro curve below as the daily read on the pre-fixed curve.
The catalyst is the election: first round on October 4 and runoff on October 25.
